business_process: Customer compute and storage data plane (SL-1, regions R1 to R6)
description: Running customer VMs, containers, block volumes, and managed databases in 18 commercial data centers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SLA of 99.99% for multi-zone resources (about 4 minutes a month); SLA credits rise to 30% of monthly fees; customers run banking, health care, and public sector workloads that stop when the data plane stops; synchronous block replication inside a zone gives RPO 0
manual_workaround: None for customers inside the failed zone; customers built for multi-zone fail over automatically; the company shifts placement to healthy zones
dependent_third_parties: Electric utilities and fuel suppliers; carriers; hardware manufacturers (spares)
dependent_people_or_facilities: Data center operations (about 2,100 staff); 18 commercial data centers
quantified_impact_basis: Loss of the largest region (R1, about 24% of SL-1 revenue) for 24 hours: SLA credits of 30% of monthly R1 fees (about $22.2 million) plus about $2.5 million of lost usage revenue
single_points_of_failure: Single region control plane per region; customers deployed in one zone have no failover

business_process: Commercial control plane, console, and public API (SL-1)
description: Provisioning, scaling, configuration changes, and console and API access for about 41,000 customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Running workloads keep running, but customers cannot scale, recover, or change anything; API SLA 99.9%; autoscaling and failover of customer applications depend on the control plane
manual_workaround: Running workloads unaffected; status page and support guidance; customers defer changes
quantified_impact_basis: SLA credits for the API and console (about $3.1 million a day at 10% to 25% credit tiers) plus deferred usage growth and support load (about $3.7 million)
single_points_of_failure: Tenant database per region; customer identity and access service

business_process: Government Cloud data plane and control plane (SL-2, region G1)
description: All SL-2 services in G1-A and G1-B for 50 government customers and about 420 DIB customers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Agencies run mission systems on G1; FedRAMP Class C (and target Class D) availability reporting (CDS-CSO-AVR); agency contracts; only two data centers, so a site loss halves capacity
manual_workaround: Agencies fail over to their own continuity sites where they have them; the company shifts load to the surviving G1 data center
dependent_systems: SYS-01 to SYS-07 (G1 instances); SYS-09 (G1 channel); SYS-11
dependent_third_parties: Electric utilities; two carriers per site; hardware manufacturers
dependent_people_or_facilities: U.S.-person G1 operations staff (about 260); G1-A and G1-B
quantified_impact_basis: SL-2 revenue of about $1.6 million a day lost or credited plus about $0.7 million of contract penalties and incident cost; federal certification and reputation impact not included
single_points_of_failure: Two data centers only; a single G1 tenant database cluster spans both

business_process: Identity and access (customer identity service and workforce identity platform)
description: Customer sign-in and API authorization; workforce SSO, MFA, and PAM for all operations
process_owner: Director of Identity and Access Management
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Every other process depends on it; administrators cannot reach management planes without PAM; customers cannot authenticate API calls
manual_workaround: Sealed break-glass accounts per platform; cached tokens keep running workloads working
quantified_impact_basis: If customer API authorization fails, most BP-02 impact plus partial BP-01 impact for workloads that call company APIs
aq1_dependency: AQ-1 staff on the legacy directory (separate failure domain)
single_points_of_failure: Workforce identity platform is a single logical service with two regions

description: Customer encryption keys, internal certificate authorities, and code signing keys held in HSMs
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Encrypted volumes and databases cannot mount without key access; certificates for internal services expire without issuance; key loss is unrecoverable, so RPO is 0
manual_workaround: None for encrypted data; certificate lifetimes give about 72 hours before internal services fail
dependent_people_or_facilities: Key management engineering; key custodians (dual control)
quantified_impact_basis: Encrypted customer resources fail to start or scale in affected regions; impact rises to BP-01 levels if keys are lost
single_points_of_failure: HSM clusters per region; key custodian quorum

business_process: Global network, DNS, and edge (DDoS mitigation and content delivery)
description: Backbone, internet connectivity, 41 edge PoPs, authoritative DNS for about 900,000 customer zones
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer sites become unreachable within minutes; DNS outages cascade to every customer service; carrier diversity exists but BGP or DNS errors are global
manual_workaround: Anycast failover between PoPs; static DNS fallback for company domains; carrier rerouting
dependent_third_parties: Carriers (two or more per data center); colocation providers for PoPs; domain registry and registrar
dependent_people_or_facilities: Network operations center; network engineering on-call
quantified_impact_basis: Global DNS or backbone failure for 24 hours affects all SL-1 and SL-3 customers: credits and lost usage at about 60% of BP-01 multi-region exposure
single_points_of_failure: Authoritative DNS configuration pipeline is global; one BGP policy repository

business_process: Object storage and backup vault services
description: Object storage, snapshots, and the immutable backup vault used by customers and by the company for control plane state
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customers keep backups and data lakes here; objects are erasure-coded across zones (RPO 0); company recovery depends on the vault
manual_workaround: Customers read from cross-region replicas where they enabled them
quantified_impact_basis: Credits on storage SLA and lost requests for the largest region; company recovery delayed if the vault is unavailable

business_process: Managed infrastructure services through fleet automation (SL-3)
description: Patching, monitoring, backup, and operations jobs on about 48,500 customer servers for about 1,210 customers
process_owner: Senior Vice President, Managed Infrastructure Services
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Customer servers keep running without the service; missed patch windows and backup jobs create risk; bank customers treat some jobs as covered services (12 CFR 53.4 four-hour threshold applies to their disruption, not to the job queue)
manual_workaround: Customers run urgent jobs through their own tools; managed engineers use customer-approved remote access
quantified_impact_basis: SL-3 revenue of about $1.3 million a day is billed monthly; the 24-hour impact is SLA credits and missed backup and patch obligations (about $1.1 million)

business_process: Legacy RMM operations for AQ-1 customers (SL-3)
description: Monitoring, patching, and scripts on about 9,500 servers of 140 SL-3 customers acquired with AQ-1
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Same as BP-08; the RMM vendor controls the platform and its recovery
manual_workaround: Customer-approved remote access; manual patching for urgent fixes
quantified_impact_basis: AQ-1 customer revenue of about $0.12 million a day plus credits and overtime
single_points_of_failure: RMM vendor platform; legacy AQ-1 directory

business_process: Software release and emergency patch deployment
description: Build, sign, and deploy host software, firmware, and guest-agent updates through CI/CD and fleet automation
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Emergency fixes for known exploited vulnerabilities and FedRAMP vulnerability timeframes (Class D: as short as 12 hours for the most severe internet-reachable cases); a stopped pipeline also blocks recovery fixes
manual_workaround: Freeze non-emergency changes; build emergency fixes on the isolated break-glass build environment with HSM signing
quantified_impact_basis: Engineering idle time and delayed releases; regulatory exposure if vulnerability timeframes are missed

description: 24x7 SOC detection, triage, and response across all regions and corporate IT
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: FedRAMP incident reports are due in 1 hour (Class C) or 15 minutes (Class D) for the most severe ratings; bank and customer notices depend on detection; blind time lets attackers act
manual_workaround: Log sources buffer locally for 72 hours; SOC falls back to EDR and platform consoles; external incident response retainer
dependent_systems: SYS-11; SYS-03; SYS-14 (security data lake copy)
dependent_third_parties: EDR vendor; threat intelligence feeds; AI triage model vendor
quantified_impact_basis: Response cost and the exposure of missing a detection window (not quantifiable in advance; minimum SOC and retainer cost shown)
aq1_dependency: RMM logs arrive as a daily batch

business_process: Customer support, status page, and incident communications
description: Support cases, the public status page, customer notices, bank and agency notices
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Bank notice "as soon as possible" after a four-hour determination (12 CFR 53.4); FedRAMP Initial Incident Reports; customer agreement notice within 72 hours; status must stay up when the cloud is down
manual_workaround: Status page runs on external Cloud provider X; phone tree and printed contact lists; notices from the out-of-band email service
dependent_third_parties: External Cloud provider X; ticketing and CRM SaaS vendor; telephony provider
quantified_impact_basis: Support overtime and the regulatory exposure of late notices (penalties not quantified)
single_points_of_failure: Customer contact data in the CRM SaaS

description: Usage metering from every region, rating, invoicing, and collections
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Metering records lost are revenue lost; invoices can be delayed a few days; SOX controls over revenue
manual_workaround: Meter records buffer in each region for 7 days; invoices delayed
quantified_impact_basis: About $13.2 million of daily usage is metered; loss of 1 hour of meter records is about $0.55 million; delay costs about $0.35 million a day in working capital and rework

description: Close, consolidation, and 10-Q and 10-K filings, including Item 106 disclosure
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: SEC filing deadlines; during quarter-end the MTD drops to 48 hours
manual_workaround: Manual close on exported trial balances
quantified_impact_basis: Rework and advisory cost; regulatory risk at quarter-end

business_process: Capacity planning and hardware supply chain
description: Forecasting, server and network purchases, receiving, and spares for 20 data centers
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Spare pools cover about 3 weeks of normal failures; G1 requires receiving checks before installation (SR-9 gap)
manual_workaround: Shift spares between regions; priority allocation to G1 and R1
dependent_third_parties: Hardware manufacturers (servers, drives, network); freight carriers
single_points_of_failure: Two server manufacturers supply about 85% of hosts

description: Payroll for 12,000 employees, onboarding and termination events that drive identity
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Payroll deadlines; termination events must reach identity governance the same day
manual_workaround: Repeat prior payroll; manual termination notices to the identity team
quantified_impact_basis: Penalty and rework cost; risk of late access removal
aq1_dependency: AQ-1 HR feed to the legacy directory is a nightly file

description: Quotes, contracts, new-account onboarding, sanctions and export screening
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Lost bookings can be recovered; screening must not be bypassed
manual_workaround: Paper contracts; manual screening by legal operations
dependent_third_parties: CRM SaaS vendor; screening data provider

business_process: FedRAMP ongoing certification and agency reporting
description: Monthly vulnerability reports, Ongoing Certification Reports, significant change notices, trust center, and the FedRAMP Security Inbox
mtd_rto_rpo_drivers: Missed FedRAMP reporting timeframes put FR-1 and FR-2 at risk; Emergency messages to the FedRAMP Security Inbox must be routed to a senior security official (AFC-CSO-EMR)
manual_workaround: Manual report generation from the GRC platform export; the inbox is monitored by the SOC as a backup
quantified_impact_basis: Staff cost of manual reporting; the real exposure is loss of certification for SL-2 and SL-1 federal revenue (about $2.2 million a day combined)
